'''''Eremochloa ophiuroides''''', or '''Centipedegrass''', is a species of grass in the family [[Poaceae]]. Used as a warm season [[lawn grass]], it forms thick [[sod]]s and spreads by [[stolons]]. 

==Overview==
The grass is medium to light green in color and has a coarse texture with short upright seedhead stems that grow to about {{convert|3|to|5|in|cm}}. Native to [[Southern China]], it was introduced to the United States in 1916 and has since become one of the common grasses in the [[Southeastern United States]] and [[Hawaii]].<ref name="auto"/> It can also be considered a weed in areas where other vegetation is desired.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://weedid.cals.vt.edu/ |title=Weeds Identification |website=weedid.cals.vt.edu}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
Centipedegrass is a low maintenance grass as it requires infrequent mowing and has low fertilization requirements.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|url=https://aggie-horticulture.tamu.edu/plantanswers/turf/publications/centipede.html|author=Richard L. Duble|title=Turfgrass | SoilCrop.tamu.edu|website=Texas AgriLife Extension Service|publisher=Texas A&M System|access-date=25 January 2023}}</ref><ref>Aaron Patton and John Boyd. [http://www.uaex.edu/Other_Areas/publications/PDF/FSA-6120.pdf "Centipedegrass."] FSA6120. University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture. ([https://web.archive.org/web/20120323160656/http://www.uaex.edu/Other_Areas/publications/PDF/FSA-6120.pdf Archived] on 23 March 2012.)</ref> Centipedegrass has medium shade tolerance and limited traffic tolerance.<ref name="auto">J. T. Brosnan and J. Deputy. [https://www.ctahr.hawaii.edu/oc/freepubs/pdf/TM-14.pdf "Centipedegrass."] TM-14. College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resources. University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa. March 2008. Retrieved 25 January 2023.</ref>

It is shallow rooted and has poor drought tolerance.<ref name="auto"/> Centipedegrass survives in mild climates without several hard freezes. With light freezes it will turn brown but recover and re-green as the [[temperature]] rises.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dollarblogger.com/lifestyle/types-of-florida-grass/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240314053515/https://dollarblogger.com/lifestyle/types-of-florida-grass/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=March 14, 2024|title=Types of Florida Grass For Your Lawn|website=dollarblogger.com}}</ref> It does well in sandy and acidic soils.<ref name="auto1"/>
